reason: Après validation des quatre créatures, Kathryn demande des paysages et de sceller les deux familles.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE premium collectible creature illustration, vertical portrait 2:3, full-bleed, ideally 1024x1536, no text or frame.
Collection: NOSFY. Predefined family: LES CIMES ÉTEINTES / THE DARKENED PEAKS, creatures born of soot and ember in black volcanic mountains. This family is visually defined by DEEP BLACK AND ORANGE EMBER, nothing else. Shared material DNA: matte charred velvet, fractured obsidian, dark smoked amber, restrained glowing orange ember fissures. A beautiful, ominous, mysterious dark universe. No moonlit silver landscape.
Art direction: dark poetic fantasy fine art, exquisitely tactile detailed painting, striking creature design and instantly identifiable silhouette. Absolutely not ordinary animal photography. Rich readable near-black forms, shadows separated through subtle black-brown values; at least three quarters of the picture very dark. Orange is concentrated into selective ember light and warm metallic reflections, not a bright overall orange background. The detail quality is extremely high in EVERY rarity; rarity changes spectacle, material finish and scale, not care.
Environment: abyssal black volcanic mountain clefts, jagged basalt spires, ancient soot, occasional dim smoky ember dust, enormous shadow masses. No white fog, no snow, no moon, no silver highlights, no blue, no purple, no green, no rainbow, no starry panorama, no bright sky. Restrained pockets of warm light reveal select details against darkness. Black-on-black remains beautifully legible on a phone.
Composition: singular coherent scene, never a grid, never a four-panel board. Keep every essential tip, face and limb within central 80 percent of canvas width and central 80 percent of height; generous breathing room for an existing external card frame. Full creature clearly visible, believable weight and organic anatomy. Depth through broad dark shapes, avoid busy background.
No typography, names, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, border, rarity moons, graphic symbols, ornamental frame or game UI. No armor, necklaces, collars, jewelry, runes, gore, skulls or humans.

COMMON LANDSCAPE CARD — LA FAILLE ARDENTE / EMBERRIFT.
Landscape-only: absolutely no creature, no animal, no face in the rocks, no people, no buildings. A quiet breathtaking place belonging to the SAME black-and-orange-ember family as a soot raven, black amber bat, ash wolf and obsidian dragon. The landscape itself is collectible and immediately recognizable.
A narrow deep fractured basalt gorge inside a black volcanic mountain. Two immense irregular walls of jet-black stone almost meet high above, leaving a tiny distant wedge of murky charcoal sky. Down the center, far BELOW the viewer, a thin winding orange ember fissure glows like a still living coal, revealing a few wet obsidian planes, layered black slate, mineral droplets and charcoal dust. It is a restrained thin seam of smoldering rock, NOT a huge bright yellow lava river and NOT a blazing inferno. Large elegant dark areas surround this exquisite thread of orange. A small unlit black stone arch naturally joins the walls in the middle distance, a recognizable signature. Multiple rock planes fade into dark warm soot haze; a few minute ash flecks catch light near the bottom only.
Intimate solemn stillness, poised diagonal viewpoint at the lip of the gorge, strong depth, magnificent finely painted geological textures where the ember grazes them, almost tactile stone and subdued copper reflections. The COMMON is beautiful through place, lighting and craft, without magical floating objects or shiny gemstone overkill. Very dark image with readable near-black tonal values and very limited orange light. A sophisticated quiet fine-art illustration, no roaring explosion, no white smoke, no moon, no silver alpine mist, no fantasy castle, no typography. Entire scene edge-to-edge portrait 2:3.

COMMON LANDSCAPE CARD — LE COL DES CENDRES / ASHEN PASS.
Only a landscape, NO creature or animal anywhere, no people, no houses, no statues, no faces in the rock. A distinct quiet landmark within the SAME black-orange ember mountain world as soot raven / black amber bat / ash wolf / obsidian dragon. Beautiful enough to cherish as a common card; all the care of a precious painting, understated spectacle.
A sinuous narrow path of cooled black volcanic ash winds up through a pass between two distinctive tall black rock needles, one broad and split lengthwise, one thin and leaning. Seen from low on the trail, the pair form an immediately recognizable monumental silhouette, almost closing around a tiny murky dark rust-colored horizon. Sharp basalt foothills and serrated mountain ridges recede into almost-black soot haze beyond the pass. Foreground ash is velvety charcoal with elegant wind-ripple textures, broken obsidian pebbles and minute restrained warm reflections. One narrow burnt-orange ember vein inside the split monolith casts a faint grazing glow onto the path and a few delicate ribbons of ash suspended in still air. Occasional dying coals partly buried in ash, not a field of bright fire. The upper three quarters remain profoundly dark, with separated black planes and no brightly luminous sky.
Palette: velvety soot black, obsidian black and a touch of ember orange only, no silver, blue, green or purple. Small areas of intricately painted material detail surrounded by calm darkness. A sublime lonely mountain passage, mysterious but inviting to explore; atmospheric fine-art dark fantasy landscape, not a volcano-disaster photograph. The identifying pair of needles, the delicate winding ash path and the hidden ember provide a different composition from a gorge. No shiny jewel waterfall, no magma ocean, no moon, no snow or bright clouds. Portrait full-bleed 2:3, no framing or lettering.
